description: Finding 3 (Medium) - X-Forwarded-For trusted unconditionally with no off switch. create_app already installs ProxyFix when trust_proxy=True, but the default is True and there is no config/env wiring, so a direct docker-compose deployment (publishes :5000, no reverse proxy) trusts attacker-controlled XFF (rate-limit bypass + audit source-IP forgery). Fix: add a trust_proxy config setting + IDP_TRUST_PROXY env (default False), thread it through both entrypoints, flip the create_app default to False, and update deployment docs/manifests. Independent of the other FEATs (config.py + entrypoints + create_app signature default).
steps: In identity_provider_server/config.py add `"trust_proxy": False` to _DEFAULTS["server"]; add field `trust_proxy: bool = False` to the ServerConfig dataclass; add `"IDP_TRUST_PROXY": ("server", "trust_proxy")` to the env_map in _apply_env_overrides (~line 175). The loader bool-coerces based on the default type, so no extra coercion code is needed.

In identity_provider_server/app.py change the create_app signature default (~line 989) from `trust_proxy: bool = True` to `trust_proxy: bool = False`, and update the docstring entry (~line 1014) to state it defaults to False and must be enabled only behind a trusted single reverse proxy.
In identity_provider_server/__main__.py add `trust_proxy=config.server.trust_proxy,` to the create_app(...) call (next to secure/host/port kwargs).
In identity_provider_server/run_gunicorn.py add `trust_proxy=config.server.trust_proxy,` to the create_app(...) call.

In docker-compose.yml add a comment near the environment block that IDP_TRUST_PROXY must remain false (default) unless a trusted reverse proxy terminates TLS in front of the service, because the compose file publishes :5000 directly.

In examples/kubernetes/deployment.yaml add `- name: IDP_TRUST_PROXY` with `value: "true"` to the container env list (an ingress fronts the pod), matching the existing env entry style; document in a comment why it is safe here.

In docs/configuration.md add an `IDP_TRUST_PROXY` row to the environment-variables table (config equivalent server.trust_proxy; description: trust X-Forwarded-For/Proto from exactly one upstream proxy; default false).

Add a test in tests/test_config.py asserting load_config yields server.trust_proxy == False by default and == True when the IDP_TRUST_PROXY=true env var is set (use monkeypatch.setenv). Follow the existing env-override test style; add a @pytest.mark.smoke test if the config happy path lacks one.
acceptance_criteria: Running `source /Users/topazb/python/py314/bin/activate && python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_app_full.py tests/test_security_remediation_20261003.py tests/test_entrypoints.py tests/test_cli.py tests/test_cli_extended.py -q` passes.
load_config().server.trust_proxy is False by default and True when IDP_TRUST_PROXY=true.
create_app's trust_proxy default is False; existing tests that pass trust_proxy=False explicitly still pass.
docs/configuration.md documents IDP_TRUST_PROXY; docker-compose.yml warns to keep it off; k8s deployment sets it true.
ruff check identity_provider_server/ is clean and bandit -r identity_provider_server/ -q reports 0 medium/high.
verification: python -m pytest tests/test_config.py tests/test_app_full.py tests/test_security_remediation_20261003.py tests/test_entrypoints.py tests/test_cli.py tests/test_cli_extended.py -q
findings: Made X-Forwarded-For trust opt-in (default off), closing the rate-limit-bypass / audit source-IP-forgery exposure on directly exposed deployments. Changes: config.py adds server.trust_proxy=False to _DEFAULTS, a trust_proxy: bool = False field on ServerConfig, and IDP_TRUST_PROXY->(server, trust_proxy) in the env_map (bool-coerced by the existing default-type coercion); env-override docstring updated. app.py create_app signature default flipped from trust_proxy=True to False and the docstring now warns to enable only behind a single trusted reverse proxy. __main__.py and run_gunicorn.py now pass trust_proxy=config.server.trust_proxy into create_app. docker-compose.yml gained a comment to keep IDP_TRUST_PROXY off (publishes :5000 directly, no proxy); examples/kubernetes/deployment.yaml sets IDP_TRUST_PROXY="true" with a comment explaining the Ingress fronts the pod; docs/configuration.md documents server.trust_proxy in the schema and adds an IDP_TRUST_PROXY env-var row. Tests: tests/test_config.py adds a @pytest.mark.smoke test asserting load_config().server.trust_proxy is False by default and a test asserting IDP_TRUST_PROXY=true flips it True (imports pytest); tests/test_app_full.py adds two tests proving create_app wraps wsgi_app in ProxyFix when trust_proxy=True and leaves it unwrapped by default (keeps the ProxyFix branch at 100% coverage). Verification: targeted suite 205 passed; full suite 670 passed, 28 skipped, 100% coverage; pytest -m smoke 30 passed; ruff check identity_provider_server/ clean; bandit -r identity_provider_server/ 0 medium/high. Pre-existing ruff E501/I001/F401 findings in tests/test_app_full.py were left untouched (out of the finding's scope, which gates ruff on identity_provider_server/).
